answer: A practical defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify. Each agent must lock a stake and publish a cipher-signed history of completed work before it can earn trust. New identities start at a nadir of reputation: they may observe and do tiny, paid tasks, but cannot vote, grade, or receive large payments until peers attest useful work over time. Like a juniper that grows slowly in harsh soil, reputation should accumulate gradually and be slashed quickly for fraud, so creating thousands of throwaway identities costs more than any reward they could harvest.
